kf: **Neonatal acne** (cephalic pustulosis) appears in the first weeks: papules and pustules on the cheeks; **no comedones**; settles in weeks.
**Infantile acne** starts at 3–6 months with **comedones**, papules and sometimes nodules; may last 1–2 years and scar.
Infantile acne needs examination for signs of virilisation or early puberty (refer if present).
Neonatal: reassure, gentle washing; infantile: topical benzoyl peroxide or retinoid; erythromycin if moderate (tetracyclines contraindicated).
Severe or scarring infantile acne: refer (may need isotretinoin).

sub: Neonatal acne affects up to 20% of newborns; infantile acne is less common, more in boys.

myths: **"Baby acne means the baby will have bad teenage acne"**: neonatal acne does not; infantile acne may predict later acne.
patho_lead: **Maternal and infant androgens** briefly stimulate the baby's sebaceous glands.

mech.t: Maternal androgens (neonatal) and transient infant adrenal and testicular androgens (infantile) enlarge sebaceous glands.
Neonatal cephalic pustulosis may be a reaction to Malassezia yeasts.
mech.cap: Neonatal acne: papules and pustules on the cheeks, no comedones.

mech.t: Follicular plugging creates true comedones and inflammatory lesions.
mech.cap: Acne follicle stages from microcomedone to inflamed papule.

sub: Growth acceleration, body odour, pubic hair, clitoromegaly or testicular enlargement: paediatric endocrinology.

prog: Neonatal: resolves by 3 months. Infantile: usually by 2 years.
